articles.title: A first look at the Verimarts marketplace
articles.body:
A catalogue works best when its categories are easy to explore. Cars, property, farm produce, electronics and general goods each have their own details worth reviewing.

Start with a category, open a listing, and compare the information that matters to you. An enquiry can then refer to the specific item rather than a vague request.
articles.cover_alt: Illustration for A first look at the Verimarts marketplace

articles.title: Questions to prepare before a vehicle enquiry
articles.body:
A vehicle listing can introduce a car, but a conversation helps fill in the gaps. Note which specifications are present and which still need clarification.

Useful questions may cover the model year, mileage, condition, service records and the opportunity to inspect the vehicle. Do not infer missing facts from photographs.
articles.cover_alt: Illustration for Questions to prepare before a vehicle enquiry

articles.title: Reading a property listing carefully
articles.body:
Property descriptions can cover different kinds of spaces. Start with the stated property type, location, dimensions and features.

If the owner has not specified whether a listing is for sale or rent, ask before making assumptions. Likewise, a missing price or measurement should be clarified directly.
articles.cover_alt: Illustration for Reading a property listing carefully

articles.title: The details that help a farm produce enquiry
articles.body: Ask what quantity the listing refers to and whether the available stock matches your needs. Avoid assuming a delivery arrangement or a harvest date that has not been stated.
articles.cover_alt: Illustration for The details that help a farm produce enquiry

articles.title: A clearer way to compare electronics
articles.body:
Electronics with similar names can have different specifications. Check the exact model, stated condition, included accessories and any information the owner provides.

Before enquiring, write down the features you need and compare them with the listing. If a specification is absent, ask for clarification rather than relying on a familiar product name.
articles.cover_alt: Illustration for A clearer way to compare electronics

articles.title: Making a useful enquiry about general goods
articles.body:
Dimensions, materials, condition and included parts can make a general-goods listing more useful. Photos can complement those details when they show the actual item.

Refer to the item title in your message and list the information you still need. This helps keep the conversation specific.
articles.cover_alt: Illustration for Making a useful enquiry about general goods

articles.title: Why actual item photographs matter
articles.body: A useful gallery gives a reader several views of the item described in the listing. Details and condition notes should support the photographs rather than leave the reader guessing.
articles.cover_alt: Illustration for Why actual item photographs matter

articles.title: From browsing to a direct conversation
articles.body:
A browsing page helps narrow a search. A detail page lets a visitor review a specific listing. The next step is a direct enquiry with the business.

Refer to the item by name and ask about any details that remain unclear. Availability and transaction terms should be confirmed directly with the owner.
articles.cover_alt: Illustration for From browsing to a direct conversation
